title: The Lord, the Judge, Before His Throne
description: The Lord, the Judge, Before His Throne in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 50, part 1, headed “The last judgment; or, The saints rewarded”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The Lord, the Judge, be-fore his throne, Bids the whole earth draw nigh, The na-tions near the ris-ing sun, And near the west-ern sky.

lines: The Lord, the Judge, before his throne,
Bids the whole earth draw nigh,
The nations near the rising sun,
No more shall bold blasphemers say,
No more abuse his long delay
Thron'd on a cloud our God shall come,
Thunder and darkness, fire and storm,
Heaven from above his call shall hear,
And earth and hell shall know and fear
"But gather all my saints," he cries,
"Their faith and works brought forth to light

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
